thread:
samir: heads up — after rotating the REDWOOD_API_KEY secret in k8s (Deployment/checkout-api) about half the pods start returning 401s to downstream services. rolling update started ~10m ago.

irene: can you paste a short log from one of the 401 pods? request id + error?

samir: here — logs show the SDK rejecting with 401 and mentioning org header missing sometimes:
```
2026-03-15T14:12:01Z ERROR request=abcd123 status=401 error=Unauthorized message=Missing X-Redwood-Org header
2026-03-15T14:12:01Z DEBUG sdk_version=0.8.4 api_key_source=env REDWOOD_API_KEY=*** masked
```

ben: are you using gunicorn with --preload by chance? that causes the master to read env and then fork, so mid-rolling secret changes won't be picked up by workers.

samir: yep, gunicorn with --preload. but only some pods show 401 while others okay — same image, same rollout.

chris: two likely combos: 1) preloaded master cached old env -> workers still using old key. 2) SDK version 0.8.4 had a caching path where client object kept API key across env changes. both could produce partial failures during staggered restarts.

irene: to reproduce locally:
1) start app with gunicorn --preload (or puma/unicorn preload equivalent)
2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=oldkey; start server
3) rotate: kubectl set secret ... -> pods with new env will get new key on container restart only. existing preloaded processes won't re-read env.

ben: quick mitigation: restart workers without --preload, or trigger full pod restart (kubectl rollout restart deployment/checkout-api) so all procs pick up new secret. also suggest upgrade SDK if you need hot-rotate behavior.

samir: is there an SDK call we can use to hot-swap keys without restart?

chris: in 0.9.0 we added a RedwoodClient.update_api_key(new_key) helper and the default client will read per-request if constructed with read_api_key_from_env=False/True flags. in 0.8.4 the default kept the key on client init. so options:
- quick: do full rollout restart (fast but causes brief capacity drop)
- medium: patch app to instantiate client per-request (reads os.environ each call) or expose endpoint to call client.update_api_key from a sidecar that watches K8s secrets
- long: upgrade SDK to >=0.9.0 and use the update_api_key hot-swap API.

samir: sample code we have currently:
```python
# app startup
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
# reused across requests
```
that explains it.

irene: note: if you create client at module import time and use gunicorn --preload, it's the same problem. move client creation into app factory or request handler or use the SDK helper.

ben: also saw some pods complaining about missing org header. double-check you set REDWOOD_ORG (old name was REDWOOD_PROJECT in some deployments) — ensure consistency. the SDK will send header X-Redwood-Org when REDWOOD_ORG present. mismatch can result in 401/403 depending on account.

samir: after doing a full rollout-restart the 401s stopped. looks like a mix of preloaded and fresh processes.

support-bot: ticket #TKT-9421 created and attached to this thread. raising to eng-infra for guidance.

eng-infra: short-term: rollout restart and confirm no more 401s. medium-term: avoid --preload unless you have a hot-key-swap mechanism; prefer mounting secret as a file + inotify sidecar that calls client.update_api_key when file changes, or move to SDK >=0.9.0.

chris: follow-up repro notes for agents/triage:
- SDK affected: 0.8.x (observed 0.8.4).
- Fixed in: 0.9.0 (adds update_api_key and optional per-request env read).
- Symptoms: partial 401s during k8s secret rotation; logs show old api_key masked but sdk_version present.
- Workarounds: full pod restart / remove --preload / instantiate client per-request / upgrade SDK.

samir: thanks — upgrading SDK + removing --preload in our next deploy. tagging this thread :thumbsup:
